az_oz_buttress.blurb: Oz Buttress is a small sector of Isolation Canyon, a quartzite canyon close to the town of Pine in central Arizona. It holds five roped climbs, a mix of three trad lines and two sport lines. Grades run from 5.8 and 5.9 up to three routes in the 5.11 range, so it suits climbers who are comfortable on harder terrain more than beginners. To reach it, follow the ledge trail along the Main Wall until the wall in front of you stops. The canyon around it has roughly 150 routes spread over several walls, so this buttress works well as an add-on to a longer day.

az_square_top_boulder.blurb: Square Top Boulder is a single standout block in the Peanut Boulders zone on Mount Lemmon, in the Santa Catalina Mountains outside Tucson, at roughly 6,000 feet. It stands north of most of its neighbours and is easy to spot thanks to its squared-off edges. Five problems are recorded, running from VB through V2, so it is friendly to newer boulderers and good for a warm-up. One of the lines is a slab that carries a PG13 note. The walk is short: go over the small hill, then cross a slab and a dry creekbed. The far end of the Peanut Boulders is generally about five minutes from the car.

az_carney_springs_wall.blurb: Carney Springs Wall is a remote wall in the Superstition Mountains east of Phoenix. It faces northeast yet catches sun into the early afternoon, even in winter. Five routes are recorded: four trad lines and a single sport line, with grades from 5.7 up to a pair of 5.11 climbs. The easier lines are multi-pitch, including two five-pitch 5.7s. The rock is light in colour and decent, though a notch below the quality found at Barks Canyon. The hike in is long and the old trail is hard to follow, so plan on about two hours to reach the base.

az_elephant_dome.blurb: Elephant Dome is a large granite dome in Mendoza Canyon, also called the Coyote Domes, west of Tucson. The five recorded routes are all trad, from 5.7 up to a 5.11 with a runout rating, with three of them in the 5.10 range. Routes are long, with some running to six pitches. This is backcountry climbing with desert views, and the rock swings from rotten to excellent, with grass and cactus on many ledges. Descents are often by rappel, and bolted anchors may lack chains, so bring extra webbing. The approach follows cairns and can be hard to track, so route-finding skill helps.

az_pyramid_the_2.blurb: The Pyramid is a small crag in the Bear Canyon section of Mount Lemmon, in the Santa Catalina Mountains near Tucson, at about 6,500 feet. The cliff is around 65 feet tall and faces mostly east, with several crack systems and a few arêtes toward the left end. Five climbs mix sport and trad, with one at 5.9, one in the 5.10 range and three at 5.11. With so few routes it is a place for a short visit rather than a full day, and the wall has been described as a spot you may have to yourself.
